id: title:jose-sequeira:key rust hogvm batches by bytecode content not array identity

review.posthog_relevance: Reduces redundant Rust VM invocations and lowers per-event latency/memory for HogQL bytecode transformations shared across HogFunction rows.
review.reason: Adds a SHA256 content hash and WeakMap cache to group queued HogQL bytecode invocations, allowing shared transformations to batch FFI crossings rather than treating each HogFunction row as a distinct program. This could reduce redundant Rust VM invocations and lower per-event latency and memory footprint for shared transformations.
review.uncertainty: The actual runtime benefit depends on the prevalence of shared bytecode in production HogQL queries, which is not demonstrated by the code alone; the implementation is bounded and does not claim systemic architectural changes.

observations.limitations: This chunk is a single, cohesive change group. No unrelated PRs detected. No adoption, incident, or effort claims are supported. No tier assignment is made; score is withheld.

observations.behavior: Adds a SHA256 content hash and a WeakMap cache to distinguish programs by bytecode content rather than array identity, and groups queued invocations by that content hash. P1.F2.H3: P1.F2.H4: P1.F2.H5
observations.posthog_connection: Allows HogQL transformations executed via the Rust VM to batch multiple events sharing the same bytecode into a single FFI crossing, regardless of whether each HogFunction row supplied a distinct array instance. This could reduce redundant Rust VM invocations and lower the per-event latency and memory footprint for shared transformations.
